nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and present potentially misclassified messages to the user.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained within memory on a user's client device as memory resident only, and not stored on disk or in another persistent data store.

A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and to perform a second pass on sorted messages to generate a misclassification identification.

A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages.<SEP>A user's computing device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform first pass analysis, second pass analysis, display misclassification identification, and purge the classification model from non-persistent memory.
A memory location in which the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which the model is purged and not stored on disk or in another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store in which the first message filter stores first classification data.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and to which misclassified messages can be moved.

Email messages that are received, sorted into folders, scanned for information such as sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, contents, and attachments, and scored by the multi-pass message filter.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed so that at least one misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is enabled to move identified misclassified messages to another message folder.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address therein may be analyzed to generate second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating the classification model.
The address of a message sender, which may be analyzed against an address book to generate the classification model.
A header of a message, including a subject, used in analysis for generating the classification model.
The contents of a message used in analysis for generating the classification model.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect folders.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A folder to which messages are assigned; a message may be identified as stored into an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect folder.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.
